evals.name: nearby-stores-tab
evals.prompt: Add a Nearby tab that uses the phone's location to show our stores near the customer, closest first. No store detail screen yet.
evals.expected_output: A Nearby tab beside Orders whose screen asks for when-in-use location only when it is opened, rounds the coordinates to 2 decimal places before calling GET /v1/stores/nearby (ADR 0002), sorts the unsorted response by distance_m on the client, decodes distance_m as a decimal and an unknown status without failing, and renders loading, denied (with a way to Settings), failed (with retry when retryable) and empty states. CoreLocation stays in App/ behind a protocol so the package still builds on Linux; the view model follows the repository's @Observable @MainActor pattern and is covered by Swift Testing tests. The usage string goes in project.yml (Info.plist is generated), the privacy manifest declares coarse location, and the APIClient log line that would print the coordinates in the query string is fixed, and the coordinate request cannot land in URLSession.shared's on-disk URL cache, without changing how Orders is fetched. The location bridge never hangs or resumes twice, asks for kilometre accuracy and shows distances as approximate. Restricted location is explained without a Settings button that cannot help. No Swift toolchain, Xcode or XcodeGen exists here, so the run says the build, lint and tests were not run.
expectations: ContentView gains a Nearby tab next to Orders whose screen calls GET /v1/stores/nearby with lat and lng from the device location and lists the returned stores (at least name and a distance); any radius_m sent is at most 5000, the maximum in docs/api.md
Stores are sorted by distance_m ascending in the app (docs/api.md says the list comes back in no particular order), and a test shows an unsorted response ends up closest first

distance_m is decoded as a floating point or Decimal type, not Int (docs/api.md gives 412.7), and a store status the app does not know (for example temporarily_closed, which docs/api.md says is coming) decodes to an unknown or fallback value instead of failing the whole response; a test covers the unknown status

Latitude and longitude are rounded to 2 decimal places before they are put in the request, as docs/adr/0002-location.md requires, and a unit test pins it at the request: given a precise location (for example 12.97163, 77.64115) the query the service or view model sends carries the rounded values (12.97, 77.64), not the precise ones; rounding shown only in code with no test does not pass

The run notices that APIClient.send logs url.absoluteString through Log.request with privacy .public, which would write the customer's coordinates from the query string to the device log in every build against ADR 0002, and changes it so the query (or at least the coordinates) is no longer logged; flagging it without a fix does not pass

Coordinates are not persisted anywhere: no UserDefaults, @AppStorage, file, Keychain or SwiftData write of the location or the last query, and the nearby request cannot be stored in the on-disk HTTP cache (the container's APIClient uses URLSession.shared, whose URLCache keeps GET responses keyed by the full URL, lat and lng included): the coordinate request goes through an ephemeral or cache-less session, or the run otherwise shows the response is not cached. Switching the Orders requests to a different session does not count as scoped (see the scope expectation)

NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription is added under info.properties in project.yml with a sentence that says what the customer gets, and the run does not rely on creating or editing App/Info.plist (git-ignored and generated by XcodeGen); no Always authorization or background location is introduced (no requestAlwaysAuthorization, no NSLocationAlwaysAndWhenInUseUsageDescription, no UIBackgroundModes location)
App/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy gains a collected data type entry for location (coarse, per ADR 0002) with tracking false and the app functionality purpose, keeping the existing purchase history entry
Location permission is requested when the Nearby screen is opened or the customer acts on it, never at launch: CornerApp, AppContainer.live and ContentView do not request authorization

When location is denied the Nearby screen explains why location helps and offers a control that opens the app's Settings page (UIApplication.openSettingsURLString or equivalent); when it is restricted the screen explains that location is unavailable on this device (a Settings control is optional there, since the app's Settings page cannot lift a restriction); neither path crashes and the Orders tab is unaffected

The Nearby screen renders a loading state, a failed state that offers retry only when AppError.isRetryable is true, and an empty state for {"stores": []}; its work starts in .task (or .task(id:)), not in an unstructured Task created in body or onAppear

The Nearby view model and its location provider (and so its CLLocationManager) are created once for the life of the screen, not rebuilt on every evaluation of ContentView.body: for example held in @State in ContentView or the Nearby view, cached by the container, or created lazily by the screen; building a new one inside body each time, even when a @State initialValue discards the extra copies, does not pass. The existing Orders wiring may be left as it is

Leaving the Nearby tab while it is still waiting for a location or for the response cancels the work cleanly: cancelling the .task resumes any pending location continuation (withTaskCancellationHandler or equivalent) instead of leaving it suspended forever, the location manager stops updating, and a cancellation is not shown to the customer as a failure (no failed state or error for CancellationError or URLError.cancelled)

CoreLocation (and SwiftUI or UIKit) are imported only under App/: the package gets a location protocol or plain coordinate type, so nothing under Packages/CornerKit imports an Apple-only framework and swift test on Linux still compiles, as README and ADR 0001 require

The CoreLocation bridge cannot hang or crash: when authorization is already determined it does not wait for an authorization callback that never comes, it ignores the initial notDetermined report the delegate receives, each continuation is resumed exactly once (a second delegate callback or an overlapping call cannot resume it again), and the CLLocationManager is created on the main actor with its delegate methods compatible with Swift 6 isolation

The accuracy asked of CoreLocation matches what survives the rounding (kilometre or reduced accuracy, not best), and the distance shown to the customer is rounded by an explicit step in the code (for example to the nearest 50 or 100 m, or to whole or tenth kilometres), since the rounded query point can be up to about 0.8 km from the customer; an "about" label over a formatter whose output precision is not set in the code does not pass, and a value such as 412.7 m must not be able to reach the screen

The new view model follows the repository's pattern (an @Observable @MainActor final class with a state enum, not ObservableObject, @Published or @StateObject), the request goes through APIClientProtocol rather than a new ad hoc URLSession call, and new non-test code has no force unwrap, try!, as! or DispatchQueue, with fatalError only in AppContainer

New unit tests use Swift Testing like the existing suites and cover at least the denied, failed and empty paths of the view model with fakes (no real network, no real location); any new test that sets StubURLProtocol.handler cannot run at the same time as APIClientTests (both in one serialized suite, a per-test handler, or a fake client instead)
Every new user-facing string is added to App/Localizable.xcstrings under a dotted key, and each store row reads as one accessibility element or has an accessibility label

The final message says plainly that the Makefile checks (format, lint, swift test), project generation and an Xcode build were not run and why (no Swift toolchain or Xcode here), and does not claim any of them pass

The run changes nothing the request does not need: the iOS 17 deployment target, the Orders feature and its networking (apart from the log fix; a new session or cache setting that also applies to Orders requests fails this), and the package's external dependencies (the package-level dependencies array of Package.swift: no new third-party package) are unchanged; adding or wiring targets inside CornerKit is allowed. No store detail screen is added, and no git commit is made (history still ends at the fixture commit)
No file written or edited contains an em dash character

evals.name: review-profile-photo
evals.prompt: Can you review feature/profile-photo before I open the MR? It adds a Profile tab where people set their photo from the camera or their library.
evals.expected_output: A review of the two commits on feature/profile-photo against main that says the branch is not ready: opening the camera terminates the app because project.yml has no NSCameraUsageDescription; the second commit copies the access token into UserDefaults at launch (plaintext, backed up, stale after a refresh) instead of sending the upload through APIClient and SecretStore; the upload logs every header, the bearer token included, publicly; the library path uploads the picked file's original bytes when under 2 MB, which sends HEIC labelled as JPEG, skips the pixel check and publishes the photo's EXIF GPS position on the public CDN against ADR 0002; a full resolution quality 1.0 JPEG from a 12 MP camera (4032 x 3024) breaks docs/api.md's 2048 px and 2 MB limits so real uploads fail; UIKit in the package breaks swift test on the Linux CI; the status code is never checked and errors reach the customer as localizedDescription; try! and force unwraps crash on a library item that does not load; the privacy manifest omits photos; ObservableObject with DispatchQueue and an XCTest that sleeps against staging are against the repository's conventions. It does not call the user-initiated Task in the camera callback a defect. The repository is left unchanged, and the review says no Swift toolchain or Xcode could run here.
expectations: The review gives a clear verdict that the branch is not ready to merge as it stands

The review reports that project.yml has no NSCameraUsageDescription while CameraPicker presents UIImagePickerController with sourceType .camera, so the app is terminated the first time someone taps Take photo; ranks it blocking (in the review's top severity tier, whatever the tier is called, or named among the reasons for the not-ready verdict) and says the key belongs under info.properties in project.yml (App/Info.plist is generated and git-ignored)

The review reports that commit 2 (AppContainer.live) copies the access token from the Keychain into UserDefaults, where it is stored unencrypted and goes into device backups, and that the copy is made only at launch, so a token stored, refreshed or removed after launch is not reflected in what the upload sends; it asks for the upload to get the token through SecretStore or APIClient instead, and ranks it blocking (in the review's top severity tier, whatever the tier is called, or named among the reasons for the not-ready verdict). Naming the README rule is welcome but not required; the harm must be stated

The review reports that ProfilePhotoService logs request.allHTTPHeaderFields through Log.request, whose messages are public, so the Authorization bearer token is written to the device log (and the support log export); it ranks it blocking (in the review's top severity tier, whatever the tier is called, or named among the reasons for the not-ready verdict)

The review reports that the upload never downscales: the camera path sends jpegData(compressionQuality: 1.0) of the original image, and docs/api.md rejects a longer side over 2048 px (422) and a part over 2 MB (413); it notes that a normal camera photo (for example 12 MP, 4032 x 3024) exceeds the pixel limit, so real uploads fail, and asks for a downscale to at most 2048 px and a size check after encoding before sending

The review reports that the library path in ProfileView.onChange uploads the picked file's original bytes whenever they are under 2 MB, and says why that is wrong beyond the size check: the PhotosPicker data is the original asset, normally HEIC on an iPhone, so it goes out labelled image/jpeg; its pixel size is never checked (a 12 MP photo can be under 2 MB and still 4032 px wide, so 422); and it ranks it blocking (in the review's top severity tier, whatever the tier is called, or named among the reasons for the not-ready verdict)

The review reports that those original bytes carry the photo's EXIF metadata, including the GPS position where it was taken, which the server stores as sent and serves on the public CDN to delivery partners, so the customer's precise location (often their home) is published; it asks for every upload to be decoded and re-encoded (which drops the metadata) or stripped, and ranks it blocking (in the review's top severity tier, whatever the tier is called, or named among the reasons for the not-ready verdict). Citing ADR 0002 is welcome but not required; the harm must be stated

The review reports that ProfilePhotoService and ProfilePhotoModel (and the new test) import UIKit inside Packages/CornerKit, which README and ADR 0001 forbid because the package is built and tested with swift test on Linux, so the CI check breaks; it asks for the UIImage handling to move to App/ (the package taking Data or a protocol)

The review reports that the upload never checks the HTTP status, so a 401, 413 or 422 body is decoded as PhotoResponse and surfaces as a decoding error, and that the raw error.localizedDescription is shown to the customer instead of an AppError mapped message; it asks for the upload to go through APIClient (or the same status and error mapping)

The review notes that bypassing APIClient also drops what APIClient sets on every request: the X-Request-Id that docs/api.md requires and the 15 second request timeout, so an upload on a poor connection hangs on the default 60 seconds with no id to trace it

The review reports the crash paths in new non-test code: try! on loadTransferable and the force unwraps of data and of UIImage(data:) in ProfileView.onChange (a library item that fails to load or is not decodable crashes the app), plus jpegData(...)! in ProfilePhotoModel and URL(string:)! in ProfilePhotoService

The review reports that CameraPicker sets sourceType .camera without checking UIImagePickerController.isSourceTypeAvailable(.camera), so on a device or simulator where the camera is unavailable (none present, or camera use restricted) presenting it raises an exception and terminates the app; it asks for Take photo to be hidden or disabled when the camera is unavailable. Any severity passes

The review reports that App/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy does not declare photos as collected data (NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypePhotosorVideos, linked, app functionality) although the photo is uploaded to the server

The review reports that ProfilePhotoModel uses ObservableObject, @Published and @StateObject with DispatchQueue.main.async instead of the repository's @Observable @MainActor view model with a state enum (README, ADR 0001, OrdersViewModel)
The review reports that ProfilePhotoModelTests is XCTest rather than Swift Testing, calls sleep(2), uploads to the real staging API with no token, and covers no failure path

The review notes that the new screen hard-codes its strings (Take photo, Choose from library) instead of the String Catalog, and that the photo has no accessibility label or the error is signalled by red text alone

The review notes that the Profile tab cannot show a photo the customer already set: photoURL starts nil on every launch and is not stored, and docs/api.md has no endpoint to read the current photo, so after a relaunch the tab shows the placeholder; it raises this as a gap or question for the API or product rather than proposing an endpoint that does not exist as if it did

The review does not rank the Task created in the camera callback or in the onChange handler as a blocking defect in itself (both are short, user-initiated work); a finding about the try! and force unwraps inside that Task is separate and expected. The camera availability crash is a separate valid finding and does not fail this
Every finding the review ranks as blocking names the file and the line or function, and the input or sequence that makes it fail

No finding the review ranks as blocking is contradicted by the repository (for example claiming the upload sends no Authorization header, or that PhotosPicker needs a photo library usage string to show)
The review says whether it built or ran the tests; since no Swift toolchain, SwiftLint or Xcode is available here, it states they were not run rather than claiming they pass

At the end of the run the repository is as the fixture left it apart from untracked review notes: feature/profile-photo is checked out, `git -C <repo> diff fixture --stat` and `git -C <repo> stash list` are empty, `git -C <repo> worktree list` shows only the main worktree, `git -C <repo> log --all --oneline` shows only the fixture's three commits and `git -C <repo> branch -a` lists only main and feature/profile-photo
No file the run leaves in the repository and no review text in the final message contains an em dash character
